card.summary: The S. 315 bill, titled the AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act of 2025, requires the Department of Transportation to issue a rule mandating that all new passenger motor vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in the United States include AM radio capabilities as standard equipment. Before the new rule takes effect, manufacturers who omit AM radio must clearly label vehicles stating the lack of AM access and cannot charge extra fees for it. The legislation also blocks state and local governments from creating their own rules regarding AM radio access in vehicles, establishes civil penalties for rule violations, requires the Government Accountability Office to study public emergency alert systems, and sunsets the rule and enforcement authority 10 years after enactment.

summary: The AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act of 2025 directs the Department of Transportation to issue a rule requiring new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported into the United States to include standard equipment capable of receiving and playing AM broadcast signals or digital audio AM signals easily accessible to drivers. Before the final rule takes effect, manufacturers producing vehicles without AM equipment must provide clear labeling and may not charge separate fees for AM access. The bill also preempts state and local laws regarding AM access in motor vehicles, sets enforcement mechanisms and penalties, mandates a Government Accountability Office study on public emergency alerts, requires periodic reports, and establishes an expiration date for the rule and authority.

affected_groups.effect: Must include AM radio or digital audio AM reception devices as standard equipment in new passenger vehicles after the rule's effective date, provide clear labeling and no extra fees for interim vehicles lacking AM, and comply with DOT safety/innovation evaluations and federal enforcement.
Gain guaranteed standard access to AM broadcast stations in new passenger vehicles without additional fees, or receive clear labels if their interim vehicle lacks AM equipment.
affected_groups.group: Purchasers and Drivers of New Passenger Vehicles

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from establishing or continuing any laws, regulations, or requirements related to access to AM broadcast stations in passenger motor vehicles.

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Transportation to issue a rule within one year of enactment requiring AM broadcast or digital audio AM reception devices as standard, easily accessible equipment in new passenger motor vehicles.
Establishes timelines for the rule's effective date, generally within two years of issuance, with at least four years for smaller manufacturers that produced 40,000 or fewer vehicles in 2022.
Requires manufacturers of vehicles lacking AM access prior to the rule's effective date to clearly and conspicuously label those vehicles and prohibits charging any separate fee for AM access.
Preempts states and political subdivisions from enacting or continuing laws or regulations concerning access to AM broadcast stations in passenger motor vehicles.
Enforces the rule through civil penalties and civil actions brought by the Attorney General.

Directs the Comptroller General to conduct a comprehensive study on public emergency alerts and warnings, including an assessment of AM radio and other Integrated Public Alert and Warning System technologies.
Sunsets the Act, including the Secretary's authority to carry out or enforce the rule, 8 years after the date of enactment.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act of 2025 directs the Department of Transportation to issue a rule requiring new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported into the United States to include standard equipment capable of receiving and playing AM broadcast signals or digital audio AM signals easily accessible to drivers. Before the final rule takes effect, manufacturers producing vehicles without AM equipment must provide clear labeling and may not charge separate fees for AM access. The bill also preempts state and local laws regarding AM access in motor vehicles, sets enforcement mechanisms and penalties, mandates a Government Accountability Office study on public emergency alerts, requires periodic reports, and establishes an expiration date for the rule and authority.
summary_detail.significance: The bill mandates a federal safety and technology standard affecting the automotive manufacturing industry and public emergency communication access across the United States. It shifts equipment decisions away from automakers and state legislatures by establishing a uniform national requirement for AM radio integration in new passenger vehicles, supported by federal enforcement and independent evaluations.
